A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CKM/CSM research, renamed Overtone in v2. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original next-step and autoregressive PDE prediction experiments, baseline comparisons, spectral analyses and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains and revises these experiments and adds original scheduling, conservation, robustness and AFNO results.

M1.justification: The underlying CKM kernel resizing, CSM stride modulation, randomized training and cyclic 4/8/16 inference remain unchanged. Overtone is a new name; expanded rollout equations document the existing procedure. Applying CKM to AFNO reuses that procedure, while alternative schedules test its existing inference flexibility.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six physical systems: Active Matter, Rayleigh-Benard, Shear Flow, Turbulent Radiative Layer 2D, Supernova Explosion and Turbulence Gravity Cooling. New diagnostics and architecture experiments use retained tasks. Expanded dataset descriptions and shear-flow generation details do not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds fixed-patch AFNO as an explicit comparator against CKM/CSM and other models in Appendix J, Table 15, and compares it with CKM-enabled AFNO. V1 investigated AFNO patch sizes and artifacts without these direct comparisons. The principal TFNO, FFNO, SineNet, Transolver, Well and CViT comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial additional protocols: schedule permutations and families, training patch options extending to 64, input contexts of 3/6/12 frames, and conservation diagnostics over 50 steps on four test trajectories. The stated learning-rate search changes from {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2} to {1e-5,1e-4,1e-3}. The more explicit aggregate training-budget description largely clarifies the existing comparison rather than establishing reruns.

E4.justification: The limited cyclic-versus-random study in v1 Appendix G.4 is replaced by broader ordering, dwell, warm-up and burst-schedule analyses, including residual spectra. V2 also adds patch-option and temporal-context robustness tests, conservation diagnostics, and artifact mitigation with CKM-enabled AFNO. Existing model-size, base-kernel and omitted-patch ablations are retained.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly discloses single-seed experiments and explains the absence of error bars in its limitations discussion; v1 does not provide this seed disclosure. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests. This is added reporting, not evidence of increased repetitions.

E6.justification: Numerous main-table values change, and substantial new results are added. For example, vanilla-ViT Shear Flow rollout CSM/fixed-patch VRMSE changes from 0.053/0.107 in v1 Table 3 to 0.0375/0.0504 in v2 Table 2, reducing the reported relative advantage from 50.5% to 25.6%. New scheduling, conservation and AFNO outcomes extend the evidence. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds a linearized Fourier-error recurrence, harmonic-lattice definitions, temporal coherence and an error-energy derivation contrasting quadratic and linear growth in Section 2 and Appendix B. This is substantial new mathematical reasoning, explicitly presented as heuristic. The original PI-resize derivation is retained and moved from Appendix A to K.

C1.justification: V1 principally claims controllable, compute-adaptive PDE tokenization with artifact reduction as an additional benefit. V2 makes coherent harmonic-error accumulation and its disruption central contributions, asserts cyclic-rollout novelty across vision/video/PDE applications, and states up to 40% lower rollout error. It also explicitly qualifies the accuracy comparison by the fixed total training-budget setting.

C2.justification: V2 adds a temporal-coherence explanation, interprets schedule ordering and persistent cycling separately from aggregate VRMSE, and uses conservation diagnostics to argue physical fidelity. It adds explicit boundaries concerning unseen patch configurations and irregular geometries, qualifies the theory as approximate, and explains when training a specialized fixed-patch model remains appropriate.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future full-code release, whereas v2 states that code is available. V2 also clarifies global batch size, uniform patch sampling and optimizer-update allocation, and documents shear-flow generation at 1024×2048 followed by downsampling to 128×256. Much of the hardware, architecture, optimizer and pseudocode documentation already existed.

R1.justification: V1 describes FlexiViT as a special case of CKM; v2 acknowledges SiCNN alongside FlexiViT as kernel-interpolation predecessors and relocates novelty toward cyclic autoregressive modulation. It adds Walrus as downstream adoption and expands physical-background citations, while removing the FrugalGPT, Matryoshka and LLM test-time-compute analogies. This substantively changes contribution positioning.

P1.justification: The paper and framework are renamed, and the abstract, introduction, contributions and conclusion are extensively rewritten around harmonic artifacts. Related work moves into the introduction, experimental sections are reordered and expanded, and appendices are substantially reorganized. These are extensive narrative changes beyond simply inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: V2 substantially revises table organization and figure presentation, adds scheduling and AFNO displays, and pairs new rollout examples with residual spectra. The original 100-step Shear Flow visualization is retained as Figure 22 rather than newly added. Equation boxes, revised captions, reordered model columns and the conference layout further change presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful empirical tests and clearer budget, seed, code and applicability disclosures. However, its newly central explanatory support contains material problems: Appendix B identifies the common harmonic lattice as Ω16 although its definition implies Ω4, and Section 3.2 claims equal token budgets for ten-step permutations whose stride counts differ as written. These issues weaken the mechanism and controlled-comparison interpretations. The benefits and harms prevent a reliable overall quality judgment.
